subject: Implementation runway & acceptance checklist for NexusHealth - staged validation and rollback
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation runway & acceptance checklist for NexusHealth - staged validation and rollback

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the chat yesterday. Sharing an initial implementation runway that folds our Mutual Action Plan (MAP) into a staged validation approach so NexusHealth can go live with minimal risk. Attached is a working MAP + acceptance checklist (Nexus_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a short canary runbook. Key highlights:

- Week 0 (Prep): account provisioning, baseline metrics capture, access reviews.
- Week 1-2 (Pilot / Canary cohort): 2% of traffic, end-to-end observability enabled, failure injection disabled, daily evals against quality thresholds.
- Week 3-4 (Ramp): progressive routing increase to 25% then 50% with automated rollback gates.
- Week 5 (Cutover): full traffic shift contingent on no regression in production evals and training completion.

Open questions for you:
1) Do you want the canary cohort to be geography-based (west region) or account-segment based?
2) Are there blackout windows we need to avoid for migration?
3) Who from Nexus will be the acceptance sign-off?

Ask: could you confirm by EOD Monday so we bake your preferences into the schedule?

Attachments: Nexus_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP + acceptance criteria), canary-runbook.pdf (runbook and rollback commands)

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation runway & acceptance checklist for NexusHealth - staged validation and rollback

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear plan and attachments. A few quick clarifications:

- Canary cohort: prefer account-segment based (pilot with ambulatory clinics first). Geography split adds complexity for our network routing.
- Blackout windows: we have a scheduled EHR upgrade in the east region May 18-19 — avoid those dates for any migrations.
- Acceptance: I'll be the primary sign-off for initial pilot; Dr. Aaron McBride (Clinical Ops) will be final sign-off post-ramp.

Also: can you add a short evaluation rubric for semantic-quality regressions? We want automated fail-fast gates tied to token-level latency and a simple precision/recall metric on extraction tasks.

Priya
Product Lead, Integrations | NexusHealth
priya.singh@nexushealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation runway & acceptance checklist for NexusHealth - staged validation and rollback

Priya —

Perfect — thanks for the answers. I updated the MAP (Nexus_MAP_v2.xlsx) to reflect:
- Canary cohort = ambulatory clinics (account-segment).
- Blackout windows noted (we'll exclude May 18-19 from migration ops).
- Acceptance flow: Pilot sign-off by you; final sign-off by Dr. McBride with checklist items.

Evaluation rubric highlights (also added to the runbook):
- Latency SLO: median token latency < 120ms, P95 < 300ms.
- Quality gate for extraction tasks: F1 >= 0.88 on the heldout set; any regression > 3% triggers auto-rollback.
- Error budget: 1% tolerated failed generations per 10k requests during canary.

Next steps:
1) I'll send a proposed two-hour training slot matrix — Marissa will coordinate ops runbooks.
2) Karthik will provision the dedicated canary pool and set up the KV cache snapshot.
3) Please confirm pilot cohort list by Monday so we can seed the prefixes and golden prompts.

Attachment: canary-runbook.pdf

Best,
Jonas
